author: Jack
title: Letter from Sir Isaac Newton in 1704 predicts when the world will end
text:
Sir Isaac Newton, a renowned scientist who is known for formulating the laws of movement and gravity, predicted the world as we know it would end in 2060.
Newton scribbled this ominous warning on a letter ships above a series of mathematical calculations more than 300 years ago.
He believed in biblical visions of the Apocalypse – in particular the struggle for Armageddon – and based his prediction on his Protestant interpretation of the Bible and events that followed Biblical history.
This propheted war is described in the last chapter of the book of Revelation and places the forces of good (led by God) against the forces of evil (led by the kings of the earth).
The Bible states that this struggle would mark the end of the world, which heralds a new era of peace through God.
Newton used mathematics and dates in Biblical history to land on the Apocalypse, with days mentioned in Scripture as years to interpret the prophecy.
For him, these time periods (especially 1260 years old) represented the time span of leaving the church and the rise of ‘corrupt’ Trinitarian religions, mainly Catholicism that a Protestant vision as a cult.
Newton studied history to determine the precise date that this deserted formally started and settled at 800 AD: the year that the Holy Roman Empire was established. The year 800 AD Plus 1,260 gave Newton the year 2060.
Sir Isaac Newton wrote an ominous prediction on a letter ships above a series of mathematical calculations more than 300 years ago and stated that the world as we would end in 2060 in 2060
“So the times and half a time are 42 months or 1260 days or three years and a half year, twelve months to a year and 30 days to a month, as was done in the calendar of the primitive year,” the 1704 reads letter.
‘And the days of short -lived animals that are placed for the years of lived (sic) kingdoms, the period of 1260 days, if dated from the complete conquest of the Three Kings AC 800, AC 2060 will end. It can end later, but I see no reason for its end. ‘
Stephen D. Snobelen, a professor for history of science and technology at the College of the University of King in Halifax, said that Newton’s prediction did not have the use of something as complicated as Calculus that he invented, but fairly easily arithmetic It can be performed by a child. ‘
Newton used 1260, 1290, 1335 and 2300 days that are found in the book Daniel and Revelations, who discuss the end and the beginning of certain times.
Instead, however, he saw them as years The ‘day-to-year principle’, a method used to interpret biblical prophecies that the word ‘day’ says symbolizes for a year.
In the book of Revelation, Christ and the Saints would intervene to set up a worldwide Kingdom of God that, according to snobbling, would rule 1000 years on earth.
Newton also believed that corrupt branches of Christianity would fall around this time, and the true gospel would be preached openly.
Before the second coming of Christ, the Jews would return to Israel, rebuild according to the Biblical prophecy and the temple.
Newton, a renowned scientist who is known for formulating the laws of movement and gravity, was also a pious Christian who believed in biblical visions of apocalypse
Although Newton did not believe that the world would cease to exist in 2060, he believed that the Battle of Armageddon would herald the return of Christ and a new era
But despite his efforts to predict the end of the world, Newton was ‘on its guard for prophetic date setting’ and ‘concerned that the failure of feasible human predictions would bring the Bible to Diskrep on the basis of divine prophecy,’ Snobbel wrote .
Newton even doubted his own prediction that the current era would end in 2060.
“It can end later, but I see no reason for its end,” he wrote.
In another prediction to the date 2060, Newton stated: ‘I don’t mention this to claim when the time will be of the end, but to put an end to the results of imaginative men who often end the time Predicting (s) by doing this, discredit the holy prophecies as often as their predictions fail.
“Christ comes like a thief in the night, (s) It is not up to us to know the times (s) seasons (who) God in his own chest.”
Nowadays it may seem contraindative to a scientist to be busy with biblical prophecies.
But according to Snobelen: ‘Newton was not a’ scientist ‘in the (modern) feeling of that term. Instead, he was a ‘natural philosopher’.
“Exercised from the Middle Ages to the eighteenth century, the natural philosophy not only included the study of nature, but also the study of God’s hand at work in nature,” he added.
‘For Newton there was no impenetrable barrier between religion and what we now call science. During his long life, Newton worked to discover God’s truth – whether it is in nature or the Scripture.
